text:
sam: FYI rolled allocator change (prefer-large-chunks=true) to reduce fragmentation. seeing KV/prefix-cache OOM spikes on multi-shard prefix workloads after rollout. attaching quick logs and profile snips.

anita: ugh, saw a couple alerts too. which cluster/instance type?

sam: eu-west-dedicated-gpu-1 (A10G pools). KV cache resident jumped after the change: ~1.2GB -> ~2.6GB on hot models. OOMs start when load hits sustained 180 req/s.

lee-runtime: do you have profiler traces? kernel selection changes can increase temp workspace requirements if we fall back to different matmul kernels.

sam: yes — ran nsys on a repro run. relevant excerpt:```
[2024-11-02 17:12:03] allocate kvcache shard0: 268435456 bytes
[2024-11-02 17:12:03] allocate workspace (cum): 1.9GB -> 3.5GB
OOM: failed to allocate 128MiB from slab (free list empty)
Backtrace: runtime::alloc -> cudaMalloc -> cuMemAllocHost?
```

marta: interesting. I also noticed heavy thrashing on free lists in the slab allocator metrics after the change. small slab sizes exhausted quickly, but large chunks sit unused.

sam: hypothesis: the allocator now carves larger contiguous buffers for kernel workspaces (good for some kernels) but that increases peak resident for prefix cache because we pin KV pages + workspace at same time. fragmentation makes small reuse impossible -> OOM.

lee-runtime: makes sense. two quick mitigations we can try: 1) temporarily cap max_workspace_per_gpu to 1GB for the pool (low risk), 2) reduce prefix-cache TTL + enforce per-model prefix cap so hot tails don't occupy all shards.

anita: +1 on cap. can we also test adjusting shard_count? more shards lowers per-shard peak allocation but increases metadata overhead.

sam: ran a sim with shard_count x2 and a lower TTL (30s -> 8s). hit-rate dropped from 0.86 -> 0.72 but mem tail reduced ~35%. tradeoff seems acceptable for tight latency SLO customers.

lee-runtime: also check kernel selection logs. if fallback to kernel_B for long sequences requires a 1.5x workspace, we could force kernel_A for short sequences to avoid cost. i can add a heuristic: if seq_len < 1024 prefer kernel_A.

marta: I can prepare a short A/B: rollout change + workspace cap (group A), vs rollback allocator change (group B). We'll measure OOMs, p95 latency, and token cost.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: started canary for rollout "allocator-prefer-large-chunks" on eu-west-dedicated-gpu-1: 2/10 nodes.

sam: good. also adding an immediate mitigation: set prefix_cache.per_model_cap=256MB on heavy models and prefix_cache.global_shard_limit=512MB. patch:```yaml
prefix_cache:
  ttl_seconds: 8
  per_model_cap_bytes: 268435456
  shard_count: 16
  global_shard_limit_bytes: 536870912
allocator:
  max_workspace_per_gpu_bytes: 1073741824
  prefer_large_chunks: true  # current change
```

anita: will those config changes survive restart? need to coordinate with Private deploys too.

sam: yes it's runtime-config for hosted; for private we'll push a recommended helm values patch.

lee-runtime: next step: I'll add a small kernel-selection telemetry flag to record chosen kernel and workspace_needed per call. we need distribution to prove hypothesis.

marta: I'll run the A/B and capture nvml/resident + slab_free_list metrics. target window 1h under synthetic burst. schedule at 12:30 UTC.

sam: action items:
- lee-runtime: add kernel telemetry + heuristic (seq_len < 1024 prefer kernel_A) — PR by EOD.
- marta: run A/B canary and collect metrics at 12:30 UTC.
- anita: coordinate Private/ Dedicated config docs and rollback plan.
- sam: prepare rollback PR (revert prefer-large-chunks) in case canary shows >5% OOM rate.

marta: noted. if canary fails I'll flip max_workspace_per_gpu to 512MB as emergency.

lee-runtime: also thinking longer term: implement buffer reuse across KV cache and workspace for read-only prefix shards (pin pages as re-usable when not actively being written). that would require refcounting but could shave peak by ~20-30%.

anita: love that. longer-term RFC would be good.

sam: thanks all — will post results after canary. :thumbsup:
